So it's be a long while since we last took a look at the rules, and Voat is a changing place.

Recently we've had a few people expressing opinions about the rules. Wih Voat's overall view on moderation, we thought it only fair to open up the floor to feedback. We're a @system sub and feel it's a good idea to do this once in a while.

I like think /v/gaming has a fair set of rules and we've always been extremely open about them and lenient on all fronts.

Of course that could just be my bias as a mod and so leave any feedback or grievances you have about our current rules (or mods!) below.

The rules are explained in detail here:

https://voat.co/v/gaming/comments/388319
/v/gaming Rule review - We need your input and feedback!

hi reacher, I know I brought this up off-hand the other day, but a rule feedback thread is a good place for wider discussion.

I've had a few cases where rule 7 was difficult to call because of its wording (No link posts to merchandise and/or unrelated products). Sometimes merchandise is directly related to gaming, like Microsoft's Xbox One price drop story. Usually voaters will post a news article talking about the price drop, but I wouldn't begrudge someone linking the product page directly.

The aim of rule 7 seems to be to prevent non-gaming gear from being advertised in /v/gaming, but allow for gaming-related gear. What do you think about adding in this exception:

Exceptions to rule 7:

Anything that's used for gaming, e.g.

  1. gaming systems
  2. gaming peripherals and attachments
  3. games themselves

That would create a clear exception for things like controller attachments, gaming peripherals, games, and systems; but would still prevent advertising on things like a Halo T-shirt, or a Splatoon smartphone case.

Also, does anyone have suggestions on how to better define, "meme" (rule 4)? We've got it pinned down as clearly as we can per the last rule discussion, but new opinions always bring new ideas. "meme" is an ill-defined concept as it is, but here is the current language:

An image, video, piece of text, etc., typically humorous in nature, that is copied and spread rapidly by Internet users, often with slight variations
Sounds like a good definition to me.

Personally I'm not a big fan of the meme ban.

At least in my opinion even with your definition pretty much anything posted on /v/gaming other than news could be considered a meme if it's been shared before.

Though I understand why you have the rule, to stop low effort content it can also lead to a throwing the baby out with the bathwater situation where actually good posts could be removed because of their format or memetic status.

Unfortunately I cannot come up with a solution to this without introducing more subjectivity to the rule which brings about an even bigger problem, the possibility of inconsistent enforcement.

So as much as I dislike it on principle, at the moment I think this definition and implementation of rule 4 is still the best we are going to get.

I appreciate the feedback. It's a pain in the butt concept to try to define in the first place. I'd love to pin this definition down further if possible, and of course we can get rid of it entirely if no one likes it any more.

This rule was implemented over a year ago when the community complained about the number of memes on the sub, and we've been struggling to more clearly define it ever since.
Yeah it's definitely a difficult balance to find.

But the effort is worthwhile :) after this thread has been up for a while we're going to sticky a discussion about rule 6 (no links to illegal content); we can put up a discussion about rule 4 (no memes) right after that if needed.

Discussion about both rules has been mixed, so it's worth talking about the pros and cons of both rules separately and make a decision as a community.

It could be that going a year without memes has cemented discussion and news as the heart of the sub, so the anti meme rule may not be necessary. And if it becomes a problem, we're always ready to adjust to meet the needs of the community.

Either way, that's some useful feedback :)
